facts.fact: The page cites example CTV campaign budgets of $1,000/month and $5,000/month as the range the framework applies to.
facts.quote: Whether you're running CTV at $1,000/month or $5,000/month, the framework here applies.

facts.fact: Adwave's own typical CPM range is $15-$35, with an average around $25.
facts.quote: Adwave's typical CPM range is $15-$35 with an average around $25.

facts.fact: The page states that a good CPM for most small business CTV campaigns on premium streaming inventory is $18-$28.
facts.quote: $18-$28 for most small business CTV campaigns running on premium streaming inventory.

facts.fact: The page claims direct attribution (QR scans, vanity URLs, survey responses) undercounts TV's real impact by 30-70%.
facts.quote: Direct attribution (TV-specific QR scans, vanity URL traffic, survey responses) will undercount TV's real impact by 30-70%.

facts.fact: The page says 10-25% lift in total conversions over baseline in the first 90 days of a well-targeted CTV campaign is typical.
facts.quote: 10-25% lift in the first 90 days of a well-targeted CTV campaign is typical.

facts.fact: The page says the baseline for conversion metrics should be captured over 4-6 weeks of pre-launch data.
facts.quote: Capture 4-6 weeks of pre-launch data on whatever your primary conversion metric is

facts.fact: The page cites most advertising research as showing viewers need 3-5 impressions to drive behavior change.
facts.quote: Most advertising research shows viewers need 3-5 impressions to drive behavior change.

facts.fact: The page says frequency below 2 means the audience isn't seeing the ad enough, while frequency above 7 means households are saturated.
facts.quote: Frequency below 2 means your audience isn't seeing the ad enough; frequency above 7 means you're saturating the same households

facts.fact: The page says 80-90% of impressions should fall in the real customer geography for a healthy CTV campaign.
facts.quote: 80-90% of impressions in your real customer geography.

facts.fact: The page states CTV completion rates on premium inventory are typically 90-98%.
facts.quote: CTV completion rates on premium inventory are typically 90-98%.

facts.fact: The page advises contacting platform support if completion rate falls below 85%.
facts.quote: if your completion rate is suddenly under 85%, contact platform support

facts.fact: The page says the strongest creative should be identified in 30-45 days before concentrating impressions on it.
facts.quote: identify the strongest performer in 30-45 days, then concentrate impressions on it.

facts.fact: The page claims pausing the weaker creative and doubling down on the winner usually improves campaign-level conversion by 15-40%.
facts.quote: Doubling down on the winner (pausing the loser) usually improves campaign-level conversion by 15-40%.

facts.fact: The page says a 20-40% branded search lift during a CTV flight is typical for well-targeted campaigns.
facts.quote: A 20-40% lift in branded search during a CTV campaign window is typical for well-targeted campaigns.

facts.fact: The page says a 10-25% direct website traffic lift during active CTV flights is typical for most local businesses.
facts.quote: 10-25% direct traffic lift during active CTV flights for most local businesses.

facts.fact: The page suggests scaling a campaign with healthy lift, frequency, and geographic match by a 25-50% budget increase.
facts.quote: Scale modestly (25-50% budget lift) and continue.

facts.fact: The guide recommends a focused weekly TV campaign review lasting 15 minutes, with at most one or two adjustments per week.
facts.quote: They're running a focused 15-minute review once a week and making at most one or two adjustments based on it.

facts.fact: The guide recommends no more than two campaign adjustments per week.
facts.quote: No more than two adjustments per week.

facts.fact: According to the guide, if 80% or more of TV impressions land in the real service area, the campaign should hold steady.
facts.quote: If 80%+ are in your real service area, hold steady.

facts.fact: The guide says a campaign with frequency under 2 means the audience isn't seeing the ad enough, and targeting should be tightened to build frequency.
facts.quote: Low frequency (under 2), modest conversion lift: your audience isn't seeing the ad enough.

facts.fact: The guide advises not optimizing a TV campaign during weeks 1-2 so the platform can settle.
facts.quote: Weeks 1-2: Don't optimize. The platform needs settling time.

facts.fact: The guide suggests the first targeting adjustment, if geographic leakage is meaningful, should occur in weeks 3-4.
facts.quote: Weeks 3-4: First targeting adjustment if geographic leakage is meaningful.

facts.fact: The guide says successful owners make 4-6 total adjustments across a 90-day campaign cycle, rather than 15-20.
facts.quote: The owners who get the most out of their campaigns make 4-6 total adjustments across a 90-day cycle, not 15-20.

facts.fact: The guide gives a typical CPM range for TV advertising of $15 to $35.
facts.quote: Should I worry if my CPM is higher than the $15-35 typical range?

facts.fact: The guide says that if CPM stays above $35 for more than a few weeks without proportional conversion lift, the advertiser should contact platform support about inventory optimization.
facts.quote: If CPM persists above $35 for more than a few weeks and isn't producing proportional conversion lift, talk to platform support about inventory optimization.

facts.fact: The guide recommends capturing 4-6 weeks of pre-campaign baseline data before launch to compare against campaign weeks.
facts.quote: Capture 4-6 weeks of pre-campaign baseline data before launch, then compare campaign weeks against it.

facts.fact: The guide recommends planning for at least 60-90 days before judging whether a TV campaign is working.
facts.quote: Plan for at least 60-90 days.

facts.fact: The guide states that direct attribution captures only 30-50% of TV's impact.
facts.unit: % of TV impact captured by direct attribution
facts.quote: Is direct attribution worth setting up if it captures only 30-50% of TV's impact?

facts.fact: The guide recommends allocating about 90% of dashboard time to the advertiser's own metrics and about 10% to competitive awareness.
facts.unit: % of dashboard time (own metrics / competitor tracking)
facts.quote: Focus 90% of your dashboard time on your own metrics; 10% on competitive awareness.

facts.fact: The guide describes a simple measurement setup of three layers, including a pre/post 4-week baseline for total conversions.
facts.quote: a pre/post 4-week baseline for total conversions

facts.fact: The guide states that a single TV measurement setup of three layers covers about 80% of what a small business needs to measure TV cleanly.
facts.quote: That's 80% of what you need to measure TV cleanly.

facts.fact: The guide says weeks 5-8 are for creative-level decisions, such as pausing clear losers and scaling clear winners.
facts.quote: Weeks 5-8: Creative-level decisions. Pause clear losers, scale clear winners.

facts.fact: The guide says weeks 9-12 are for performance reading and scaling decisions, with most adjustments made at the end-of-cycle decision point.
facts.quote: Weeks 9-12: Performance reading and scaling decisions.

facts.fact: The guide says the 90-day clean read usually comes at the 90-day mark when pre/post baseline comparisons stabilize.
facts.quote: Most clean reads happen at the 90-day mark when pre/post baseline comparisons stabilize.
